alignments.note: Waw of the consecutive form takes And (rule 14); the verb takes the verb.

Imperative rendered by the English idiom Get thee up. The thee is not a supplied object but part of the reflexive motion idiom the imperative is rendered by, so it stays in the verb's unit (rule 44); up is a phrasal particle, so the head stays on the lexical verb Get rather than moving to it.
Preposition rendered into.
Construct noun keeps only its own word; the relational of goes to the rectum under rule 19.
Article on the toponym: the ASV writes no the for the phrase, which is determined by this instead, so the article is unrepresented (rule 29).
Nomen rectum takes the construct relation's of, headed on the noun (rules 19, 24).
Agreement article on the demonstrative: the phrase's single determiner this is what the demonstrative pronoun itself renders, so that morpheme takes it and this article is unrepresented (rule 41).
Demonstrative pronoun takes the written this (rule 41).
Conjunction rendered and (rule 14).
Imperative rendered behold.
Definite object marker: the ASV writes the object bare, spending no word on the object relation (rule 16).

Construct noun; no article morpheme stands in the chain, so the supplied the joins the construct (rule 29), headed on the noun.

review_notes: The phrase har hā-ʿăḇāriym ha-zzeh carries three determiner-bearing morphemes but the ASV writes one determiner, this. It is placed on the demonstrative pronoun under rule 41, leaving both articles unrepresented; the competing reading would give this to the agreement article, but rule 41 gives a written demonstrative to the demonstrative pronoun standing in the phrase before an article.

Get thee up: the pronoun is read as part of the imperative's English idiom rather than as a supplied object that would be added under rule 44. The competing reading marks thee added; the idiom is not an object of the intransitive verb of ascent, so it is kept in the verb's unit.
